pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What might happen if the water for a drip system is dirty? (1 mark)
   A. The plants will grow faster
   B. The water will taste better
   C. The holes may block
   D. The bucket will be lighter

2. Which of these is a fuel used at home for cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Cloth
   B. Glass
   C. Sand
   D. Charcoal

3. Which is the safest way to make holes or dig for scarecrow parts? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an adult to help
   B. Use bare hands on sharp tools
   C. Use broken glass
   D. Play with the tools

4. Why should a scarecrow be moved every few days? (1 mark)
   A. It gets too hot
   B. The pole is too heavy
   C. Animals get used to one that never moves
   D. It grows

5. What should the scarecrow pole be like? (1 mark)
   A. Very short
   B. Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   C. Loose so it can fall over
   D. Made of glass

6. Which is a way of conserving wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Protecting their homes such as forests
   B. Selling them
   C. Cutting down all trees
   D. Setting fires in the bush

7. Where is a scarecrow best placed? (1 mark)
   A. In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
   B. At the river
   C. Far from the crop
   D. Inside the house

8. Which tool gives gentle watering of a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. Hose without a nozzle
   B. Watering can with a fine rose
   C. Cup thrown from far
   D. Bucket poured fast

9. Why is it best to plant fruit varieties that suit the local climate? (1 mark)
   A. They need no water
   B. They never get pests
   C. They cost more
   D. They grow and fruit better

10. Which of these is a sign of a healthy young fruit plant? (1 mark)
   A. Yellow and dry leaves
   B. Rotten stem
   C. Fallen stem
   D. Green leaves and steady growth

11. Which of these is a climbing fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Grapes
   B. Mango
   C. Orange
   D. Guava

12. What is a seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A dry stick
   B. A ripe fruit
   C. A young plant grown from a seed
   D. A type of soil

13. Why does passion fruit need a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. It eats insects
   B. It is a tree
   C. It grows underground
   D. Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone

14. Why is a meal of only chips not balanced? (1 mark)
   A. It lacks body-building and protective foods
   B. It has no energy
   C. It has too many vegetables
   D. It has too much protein

15. Why should food be dry before it is put into hot oil? (1 mark)
   A. Water makes oil colourless
   B. Water makes food sweet
   C. Water makes oil cold
   D. Water makes hot oil splash

16. How do you test if boiled potatoes are cooked? (1 mark)
   A. They are still very hard
   B. They turn green
   C. They float
   D. A fork goes in easily

17. Should you share a toothbrush? (1 mark)
   A. Only at school
   B. Yes with friends
   C. No
   D. Yes with family

18. About how long should you rub hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. About 5 minutes
   B. About 20 seconds
   C. About 1 second
   D. Not at all

19. Which disease can result from drinking unsafe water? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Cholera
   C. Toothache
   D. A cut

20. What is a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A simple hand-washing device made from a container
   B. A toothbrush
   C. A type of soap
   D. A cooking pot

21. Where should you start mopping? (1 mark)
   A. Next to the door
   B. At the corner farthest from the door
   C. Outside
   D. In the middle

22. Why is a damp cloth used for dusting? (1 mark)
   A. It hides dust
   B. It scatters the dust
   C. It traps the dust
   D. It dries the room

23. Which refuse can be put in the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings
   B. Plastic bottles
   C. Batteries
   D. Tins

24. Which method uses water and a mop? (1 mark)
   A. Burning
   B. Dusting
   C. Sweeping
   D. Mopping

25. Which method wipes dust from furniture? (1 mark)
   A. Mopping
   B. Burning
   C. Dusting
   D. Sweeping

26. Why should rubber boots not be dried in very strong heat? (1 mark)
   A. They grow
   B. They get heavier
   C. They become cleaner
   D. The rubber can crack

27. What should you do with cleaning materials afterwards? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them on the floor
   B. Drink them
   C. Give to animals
   D. Store them away from small children

28. How should gumboots be dried? (1 mark)
   A. In a closed cupboard while wet
   B. Under a heavy weight
   C. Upside down in a shady, airy place
   D. Beside a hot fire

29. What should you do at the end of a sewing lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them
   B. Hide them
   C. Throw them
   D. Count the needles and pins

30. Why do we knot the end of the thread? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. So it does not pull through the cloth
   C. To colour it
   D. To make it stronger

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three reasons why nails should be kept short and clean. (3 marks)

32. Why should kerosene never be poured onto a fire? (2 marks)

33. Give three ways of disposing of refuse safely. (3 marks)

34. Why should fruit be washed before it is eaten? (2 marks)

35. Give three uses of sheep. (3 marks)

36. Describe how a group can share the work of growing a fruit tree at school. (4 marks)

37. Give two ways of protecting fruits from birds and monkeys without killing them. (2 marks)

38. Why should plastic not be burnt? (2 marks)

39. Why must a passion fruit plant have a trellis? (2 marks)

40. State two ways of making drinking water safe. (2 marks)

41. List four basic needs of domestic animals. (4 marks)

42. State the difference between boiling and shallow frying. (2 marks)

43. Give three mistakes to avoid when sowing tiny seeds. (3 marks)

44. Explain how stagnant water around the home can lead to disease and how to prevent it. (4 marks)

45. Explain four ways germs can enter the body. (4 marks)

46. Give two reasons why goats are suitable for dry areas. (2 marks)

47. Name three PPE items and what each protects. (3 marks)

48. Give three peaceful ways of protecting crops from birds and animals apart from a scarecrow. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — The holes may block
   Dirt gets stuck in tiny holes.

2. D — Charcoal
   Charcoal is burnt to give heat.

3. A — Ask an adult to help
   Safety comes first.

4. C — Animals get used to one that never moves
   Animals learn that something still is harmless.

5. B — Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   A loose pole falls in the wind.

6. A — Protecting their homes such as forests
   Protecting habitats lets animals live.

7. A — In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
   It must be seen by the animals that come to the crop.

8. B — Watering can with a fine rose
   Fine spray does not wash seeds away.

9. D — They grow and fruit better
   Wrong climate gives poor growth.

10. D — Green leaves and steady growth
   Healthy plants grow green.

11. A — Grapes
   Grapes grow on vines.

12. C — A young plant grown from a seed
   A seedling is a young plant.

13. D — Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone
   Climbers need supports.

14. A — It lacks body-building and protective foods
   Chips give mainly energy.

15. D — Water makes hot oil splash
   Splashing oil can burn.

16. D — A fork goes in easily
   Soft potatoes are ready.

17. C — No
   Toothbrushes carry germs.

18. B — About 20 seconds
   This is long enough to clean properly.

19. B — Cholera
   Cholera spreads through dirty water.

20. A — A simple hand-washing device made from a container
   A tippy tap uses little water.

21. B — At the corner farthest from the door
   You do not step on the clean floor.

22. C — It traps the dust
   Damp cloths hold dust.

23. A — Vegetable peelings
   Organic waste rots.

24. D — Mopping
   Mopping washes floors.

25. C — Dusting
   Dusting removes dust from surfaces.

26. D — The rubber can crack
   Heat damages rubber.

27. D — Store them away from small children
   Keep them safe.

28. C — Upside down in a shady, airy place
   This drains water and protects the rubber.

29. D — Count the needles and pins
   Counting ensures none is lost.

30. B — So it does not pull through the cloth
   A knot anchors the thread.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs hide under nails, worm eggs are found there, and long nails can scratch and cause injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: It catches fire quickly and can burst into flames and burn people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for catching fire, 1 mark for danger.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Compost organic waste; put other waste in a bin with a lid and take it to a collection point; reuse or recycle paper, plastic and glass; wrap broken glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remove dirt and germs so it is safe to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for germs or safety.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mutton, wool (some breeds), skins, manure, income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a chart with jobs such as watering, weeding, mulching and recording; take turns each week; check the plant daily; record dates of flowers and fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity or arrangement.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cover with nets, use scarecrows, noise or shiny objects (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: The smoke is harmful to health and the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harmful smoke, 1 mark for the environment or health.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Its stem is soft and cannot stand, so the trellis supports it as it climbs and spreads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soft stem, 1 mark for support.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boil and cool it covered; use a filter or treatment tablets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean water, enough feed, clean shelter, health care and kind handling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each need.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boiling cooks food in bubbling water. Shallow frying cooks food in a thin layer of hot oil in a pan.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Leaving big lumps in the seedbed, sowing too deep, sowing too thick without thinning, or watering strongly (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mosquitoes breed in it and spread malaria. Empty tins and tyres, fill puddles, and drain water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for breeding, 1 mark for disease, 2 marks for prevention.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Through the mouth from dirty hands, dirty food, dirty water, and through cuts or feet without shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: They eat leaves, shrubs and grass, and can live where cattle find little to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Nets, fences, noise makers, shiny objects, guarding at the time animals come (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.
